incoming.explanation: The disjoint-families finding is read off the matrix and was not visible before it.
Six rows of the matrix are not readable without the reasoning behind their scores.

outgoing.explanation: The matrix is the specification applied; it has no meaning apart from it.

shortLabel: The matrix: fourteen live candidates scored, and three record-state rows that cannot be scored at all

sources.alignmentNote: The matrix is a scoring frame over evidence cited on each candidate's own unit; it introduces no new record.
sources.locator: The candidate pool the matrix scores is the output of the July 2026 parent, child, mother and marriage sweeps across this and the county sets

statement: Scoring every non-zero candidate against the fifteen attributes on a five-level scale - strong, soft or partial, unknown or untested, absent, contradicted - puts Candidate B, Ackworth, Cheddington 1608, C(ii) Berkhamsted, Candidate D, the Epping and North Weald line, Hitcham, the Newgate apprentice, Weston Turville, the Bucks/Herts/Beds group, A(1603) Stewkley, Gurley of Westminster, C(i) Berkhamsted and Stewkley 1611 side by side, with the eliminated Eythorne household scored as calibration. Laying them out side by side is what made the structural finding visible; it was not apparent from any candidate's own file. The three leading probability rows - no record survives or is indexed anywhere, documented but never assembled into a person, and documented but in a source or class not yet searched - are not people and cannot be scored on the matrix at all, and between them they hold about 44 percent.

unit.title: Identity — the shape, the matrix, and the two families
